outcomes.question: In general, how does a tax treaty affect withholding tax for non-resident payments?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### IRAS — Corporate income tax

**Status:** Evidence verified

**Effect of a tax treaty on withholding-tax applicability** (party in scope: Company)
- **IRAS rule explanation:** IRAS guidance shows that a Singapore DTA can change withholding-tax treatment for covered income, but it does not establish a blanket exemption for every payment to a non-resident. The relevant result depends on the recipient’s tax residence, the payment or income category, the applicable treaty article and, for services, where the work is performed and whether the treaty’s permanent-establishment rules are met. IRAS notes that some DTAs contain a separate technical-services article, so a general business-profits rule may not settle that category. The retained source provides examples for non-resident company services and interest; it does not establish a treaty-specific rate or outcome for an unspecified payment. Confirm the recipient, payment type and relevant DTA before concluding. [IRAS | Payments that are subject to withholding tax](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/withholding-tax/payments-to-non-resident-company/payments-that-are-subject-to-withholding-tax)

**Source:** IRAS | Payments that are subject to withholding tax (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Effect of a tax treaty on withholding-tax applicability): If the non-resident company resides in a jurisdiction that has concluded a DTA with Singapore, the provisions under the DTA apply.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Effect of a tax treaty on withholding-tax applicability): If the company is a resident of a jurisdiction with which Singapore has an Avoidance of Double Tax Agreement (DTA), the DTA may provide for relief from double taxation, depending on the provision of the DTA.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Effect of a tax treaty on withholding-tax applicability): For DTAs which contain a separate Article on Technical Services (e.g. the Singapore-Malaysia DTA), the tax to be withheld depends on the tax rate stated in this Article. However, if the non-resident company has a permanent establishment in Singapore, the provisions of the Business Profits Article apply instead.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Effect of a tax treaty on withholding-tax applicability): This rate may be reduced if relief is available under an applicable tax treaty.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Effect of a tax treaty on withholding-tax applicability): If the non-resident company resides in a jurisdiction that has concluded a DTA with Singapore, the provisions under the DTA apply.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Effect of a tax treaty on withholding-tax applicability): If the company is a resident of a jurisdiction with which Singapore has an Avoidance of Double Tax Agreement (DTA), the DTA may provide for relief from double taxation, depending on the provision of the DTA.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Effect of a tax treaty on withholding-tax applicability): For DTAs which contain a separate Article on Technical Services (e.g. the Singapore-Malaysia DTA), the tax to be withheld depends on the tax rate stated in this Article. However, if the non-resident company has a permanent establishment in Singapore, the provisions of the Business Profits Article apply instead.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Effect of a tax treaty on withholding-tax applicability): This rate may be reduced if relief is available under an applicable tax treaty.
- Official source: [IRAS | Payments that are subject to withholding tax](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/withholding-tax/payments-to-non-resident-company/payments-that-are-subject-to-withholding-tax)

sources.documentTitle: IRAS | Payments that are subject to withholding tax
sources.paragraphOrSection: Withholding Tax on Payments to Non-residents
sources.sourceText:
If the non-resident company resides in a jurisdiction that has concluded a DTA with Singapore, the provisions under the DTA apply.

If the company is a resident of a jurisdiction with which Singapore has an Avoidance of Double Tax Agreement (DTA), the DTA may provide for relief from double taxation, depending on the provision of the DTA.

For DTAs which contain a separate Article on Technical Services (e.g. the Singapore-Malaysia DTA), the tax to be withheld depends on the tax rate stated in this Article. However, if the non-resident company has a permanent establishment in Singapore, the provisions of the Business Profits Article apply instead.

This rate may be reduced if relief is available under an applicable tax treaty.
